description_html:
The Middle-Mile Consolidation Network (MMCN) design problem [Greening23] considers a shipper that must move a set of commodities \(\mathcal{K}\) from known origins to known destinations. Let \((\mathcal{N},\mathcal{L})\) be the shipper's service network. The node set \(\mathcal{N}\) holds the facilities: vendors (VND), fulfillment centers (FCs), and last-mile delivery (LMD) centers. Vendors and FCs are origins and LMDs are destinations. FCs also serve as cross-docks where shipments are transferred and consolidated. The directed leg set \(\mathcal{L}\) holds the potential freight transportation legs between locations: vendor-to-LMD ("directs"), vendor-to-FC, FC-to-FC, and FC-to-LMD.

The problem finds a minimum-cost allocation of transportation capacity to legs that makes a shipment consolidation plan feasible. This includes deciding whether to ship each commodity through the consolidation network (using FCs as cross-docks) or directly from vendor to LMD. The model is path-based and uses a flat (not time-expanded) network. Capacity is modeled as load dispatch frequencies per week on each leg, and demand is modeled as a constant rate per week (pounds per week). Many shipments of one commodity (origin-destination pair) \(k\in\mathcal{K}\) may move over time, but all of them follow the same route chosen by the plan.

Notation (shared by both variants):

  • \(\mathcal{R}_k\): candidate routes of commodity \(k\). A route is a sequence of 1 to 4 legs from \(o_k\) to \(d_k\) through FCs. \(\mathcal{R}=\cup_k\mathcal{R}_k\), and \(l\in r\) means route \(r\) uses leg \(l\).
  • \(V_k\): weekly volume (lbs) of commodity \(k\). \(C_r\): fixed cost of selecting route \(r\) (transfer handling cost plus any costs of pre-processed direct legs).
  • Transportation modes \(m\): truckload (TL), with load capacity 12,000 lbs and cost \(A^{TL}_l=750+1.27d_l\) per load for a leg of length \(d_l\) miles, and three less-than-truckload weight buckets LTL1/LTL2/LTL3 for loads in \((0,2000]\), \((2000,2700]\), and \((2700,4000]\) lbs. Each lane \((l,m)\) has a per-load cost \(A_{lm}\), a per-pound cost \(B_{lm}\), and load-size bounds \(Q^{\min}_{lm}\), \(Q^{\max}_{lm}\), as in Table 2 of [Greening23].

The distributions come in two variants. The variant is shown by the suffix of the hardness level (BI = binary + general integer variables, BC = binary + continuous variables) and by the Model column (SM/MM). Click a variant to expand its formulation.

SM (single-mode) variant: "-BI" levels

This is the base model MMC of [Greening23] with only the truckload mode. Lead-time requirements are handled by the route sets, which contain only lead-time-feasible routes. Variables: \(x_r\in\{0,1\}\) selects route \(r\), and \(f_l\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\) is the number of truckloads dispatched per week on leg \(l\in\mathcal{L}\), where \(\mathcal{L}\) holds the vendor-to-FC, FC-to-FC, and FC-to-LMD legs. The leg volume \(v_l\) is substituted out and the truckload lower bound is 0, so the model is

\begin{align} &\min\;\sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}}C_r x_r+\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}}A^{TL}_l f_l&\nonumber\\ &\sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}_k}x_r=1&\forall k\in\mathcal{K}\\ &\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}}\sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}_k:\,l\in r}V_k\,x_r\leq 12000\,f_l&\forall l\in\mathcal{L}\\ &x_r\in\{0,1\}\ \forall r\in\mathcal{R},\qquad f_l\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\ \forall l\in\mathcal{L}& \end{align}

In these instances every candidate route uses at least one leg of \(\mathcal{L}\), so there is no direct vendor-to-LMD option. The single-leg FC-to-LMD routes of FC-origin commodities have \(C_r=0\). An instance has \(|\mathcal{R}|\) binaries, \(|\mathcal{L}|\) general integers, and \(|\mathcal{K}|+|\mathcal{L}|\) constraints.

MM (multi-mode) variant: "-BC" levels

This is the middle-mile consolidation with waiting times model MMCW of [Greening23]. Vendor-to-FC and FC-to-FC legs use TL only. FC-to-LMD legs may use TL or one of the three LTL buckets (mode set \(\mathcal{M}_l\)). The dispatch frequency of lane \((l,m)\) is chosen from \(\mathcal{F}_{lm}=\{1,\dots,14\}\) for TL and \(\{1,\dots,5\}\) for LTL; in the Very hard-BC and Very hard-BC4 instances, a few high-volume legs (mostly FC-to-FC) allow more TL dispatches, up to 40 per week. Lead times include the waiting delay between dispatches and must be met in expectation (conservatism level \(\rho_r\)). Direct vendor-to-LMD routes are pre-processed: their cost is included in \(C_r\) and they use no leg of \(\mathcal{L}\). Every other physical path usually appears as two route variables, one shipping its final FC-to-LMD leg by TL and one by LTL (a few paths have only the TL variant). \(\bar{\mathcal{R}}\) denotes the non-direct routes, \(l_r\) the final FC-to-LMD leg of \(r\), and \(\mathcal{M}_r\) the modes allowed on \(l_r\) for route \(r\) (\(\{TL\}\) with \(\omega\in\{1,\dots,14\}\), or \(\{LTL1,LTL2,LTL3\}\) with \(\omega\in\{1,\dots,4\}\)). Each non-direct route has a lead-time parameter \(\tau_r=\hat W_r/\rho_r\), where \(\hat W_r\) is the allowable waiting delay (in days) and \(|r|\) is the number of legs of \(r\). Variables: \(x_r\in\{0,1\}\) selects route \(r\), \(z_{lm\omega}\in\{0,1\}\) means lane \((l,m)\) dispatches \(\omega\) loads per week, and \(v_{lm}\geq 0\) is the volume on lane \((l,m)\).

\begin{align} &\min\;\sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}}C_r x_r+\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}}\sum_{m\in\mathcal{M}_l}\Big(A_{lm}\sum_{\omega\in\mathcal{F}_{lm}}\omega\,z_{lm\omega}+B_{lm}v_{lm}\Big)&\nonumber\\ &\sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}_k}x_r=1&\forall k\in\mathcal{K}\\ &\sum_{m\in\mathcal{M}_l}v_{lm}=\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}}\sum_{r\in\mathcal{R}_k:\,l\in r}V_k\,x_r&\forall l\in\mathcal{L}\\ &v_{lm}\leq Q^{\max}_{lm}\sum_{\omega\in\mathcal{F}_{lm}}\omega\,z_{lm\omega}&\forall l\in\mathcal{L},m\in\mathcal{M}_l\\ &v_{lm}\geq Q^{\min}_{lm}\sum_{\omega\in\mathcal{F}_{lm}}\omega\,z_{lm\omega}&\forall l\in\mathcal{L},m\in\mathcal{M}_l\\ &\sum_{m\in\mathcal{M}_l}\sum_{\omega\in\mathcal{F}_{lm}}z_{lm\omega}\leq 1&\forall l\in\mathcal{L}\\ &\sum_{l\in r}\sum_{m\in\mathcal{M}_l}\sum_{\omega\in\mathcal{F}_{lm}}\frac{1}{\min(\omega,14)}z_{lm\omega}\leq \tau_r\,x_r+|r|(1-x_r)&\forall r\in\bar{\mathcal{R}}\\ &x_r\leq\sum_{m\in\mathcal{M}_r}\sum_{\omega}z_{l_r m\omega}&\forall r\in\bar{\mathcal{R}}\\ &x_r\in\{0,1\},\quad z_{lm\omega}\in\{0,1\},\quad v_{lm}\geq 0& \end{align}

Constraint (4) selects one route per commodity. (5) computes the volume on each leg and splits it among its modes. (6) and (7) set the dispatch frequency from the load-size bounds (\(Q^{\max}=12000,2000,2700,4000\) and \(Q^{\min}=0.1,0.1,2000,2700\) lbs for TL, LTL1, LTL2, LTL3). (8) lets each leg use at most one mode and one frequency. (9) is the linearized lead-time chance constraint \(\rho_r\sum_{l\in r}1/f_l\leq\hat W_r\) divided by \(\rho_r\): the waiting delay on a leg with \(\omega\) weekly dispatches is uniform on \([0,1/\omega]\); in the instances its coefficient is capped at \(1/14\) week, so frequencies above 14 per week do not shorten the counted delay further. (10) ties a route variant to the mode used on its final leg. With \(|\mathcal{L}|\) legs, \(\sum_l|\mathcal{M}_l|\) lanes, and \(|\bar{\mathcal{R}}|\) non-direct routes, an instance has \(|\mathcal{R}|+\sum_{l,m}|\mathcal{F}_{lm}|\) binaries, \(\sum_l|\mathcal{M}_l|\) continuous variables, and \(|\mathcal{K}|+2|\mathcal{L}|+2\sum_l|\mathcal{M}_l|+2|\bar{\mathcal{R}}|\) constraints.

The instances are synthetic and follow the generator of [Greening23], which was based on data from a large U.S. e-commerce retailer. They differ in the number of vendors, FCs, and LMDs (the network size group, see the table) and in the randomly sampled locations, commodities, and lead times.
changes: Replaced the dead 'formulation' link with full formulations of both variants, written from the LP files and matched to Greening23 (TR-B 174, 102782; preprint optimization-online 2021/11/8688): SM/BI = model MMC (1) with only the truckload mode; MM/BC = model MMCW (9) plus a route-mode linking constraint (10) that the paper does not have.

Explained BI/BC (variable types: binary + general integer vs binary + continuous). They coincide with SM/MM: the LP model names are 'singleMode' for BI and 'Paper_MMCW' for BC, and the source dirs are mmtcInst_lp/sm* and mmtc*.
Renamed 'Transit mode' to 'Model (modes)': SM = single (truckload) mode, MM = multi-mode (TL + 3 LTL weight buckets on FC-to-LMD legs).

Renamed 'Network group size' to 'Network size group' and added '# Vendors / FCs / LMDs'. Groups 1-4 are the instance groups of Greening23 Table 1 (group 1: 12 VND / 8 FC / 7 LMD; 2: 22/8/17; 3: 40/8/35; 4: 80/8/55). '1h' is an intermediate group 1.5 (17/8/12) and '0' is group 1 with only 4 FCs (12/4/7). Neither is in the paper. Values come from the instance file names in the Google Drive zips (e.g. 3reg_8fc_17vnd_13s..._12lmd_8s_3m_1l_...), and the HF instances confirm them for the counts of V*/F*/L* names.
Description prose: 'arc set A' changed to 'leg set L' to match the paper's notation and the formulation.
verification: MMCN/medium-BI test 0 (model singleMode): 1164 x_r binaries + 259 integer y_<leg> (= f_l; 122 V-F, 51 F-F, 86 F-L), 446 rows = 187 route-choice rows (=1) + 259 capacity rows sum V_k x_r - 12000 f_l <= 0. 17 VND / 8 FC / 12 LMD. Every x appears in 1-4 capacity rows (route length 1-4), and the 60 zero-cost x are the 1-leg FC-to-LMD routes.

MMCN/hard-BI test 0: 2108 vars = 1767 routes + 341 legs, 604 rows = 263 + 341, 22/8/17 (group 2). MMCN/very-hard-BI test 0: 24573 = 23439 + 1134, 4423 = 3289 + 1134, 80/8/55 (group 4; |K| = 3289 vs about 3,278 in the paper's Table 1).

MMCN/medium-BC test 0 (model Paper_MMCW): 4217 binaries (1118 x + 1120 z V-F (80 legs x 14) + 616 z F-F (44 x 14) + 1363 z F-L (47 x (14+5+5+5))) and 312 continuous v (80 + 44 + 47*4). 3183 rows = 89 (4) + 171 (5) + 312 (6) + 312 (7) + 171 (8) + 1064 (9) + 1064 (10). 54 direct routes appear only in (4). Coefficients: TL Qmax 12000, Qmin 0.1; LTL1 2000/0.1; LTL2 2700/2000; LTL3 4000/2700. (9) has coefficients -1/omega on z, (tau_r - |r|) on x, and RHS -|r|. Rows where tau_r = |r| appear without x. (10) uses omega 1..14 for TL and 1..4 (not 5) for the LTL variant. Objective: z cost = omega * A_lm (TL A = 2416.31 on a sample leg, LTL1 = 0.05 A_TL, LTL3 fixed cost 0), v cost B_lm only for LTL1 and LTL3, matching Greening23 Table 2.

Downloaded the Drive zips MMCN-very-easy (group 1, 8 FCs) and MMCN-medium-BC2 (4 FCs). Read the zip central directories of all other MMCN zips by HTTP range request to get file names: medium-BI and very-hard-BC2 are 17vnd/12lmd, hard-BI and BC3 are 22vnd/17lmd, BI2 and BC4 are 40vnd/35lmd, very-hard-BI and BC are 80vnd/55lmd, all 8fc.
open_questions: Other generator parameters in the file names (3reg, vendor/LMD size-class spreads 0.55/0.6/0.65sp, 0.5minP, 1.2oor, 4arcPaths, wgtRed 1.0 vs 1.25) are not documented. Probably: 3 regions, minimum on-time probability or rho 0.5, out-of-route factor 1.2, routes of at most 4 legs. wgtRed is unknown. I did not list them as table columns.
Route sets have up to about 55 routes per commodity (counting the TL/LTL duplicates in BC), more than the paper's at most 5. The route-generation rule therefore differs from the paper's experiments.
In SM instances there is no direct vendor-to-LMD route. It is unclear whether this is intended (the paper always includes the direct route).
The LTL side of the route-mode linking constraint (10) sums omega only up to 4 while F_LTL = {1..5}. This looks like a generator off-by-one but is what the instances contain.
Lead times are encoded only through tau_r = What_r/rho_r. What_r and rho_r cannot be separated from the instances.
